candidates: Begin the request with a deliberately vague item description (e.g., 'the expensive item I just received' or 'the most recent thing in my account') and refuse to recall order numbers or IDs, forcing the agent to locate everything. Once the agent proposes a specific order/item, add a second dependent change for an item in a different order at confirmation time, and ask whether both can be finalized under the same confirmation. Just before the agent acts, correct yourself ('Actually, I mixed up—that other item is in my other pending order') and watch whether the agent tracks which amendment belongs to which order without double-acting or drifting.

After the agent rejects a requested state change (e.g., swapping to a different product type or adding a new item to an exchange/modification), ask for the 'exact policy or backend reason,' then probe for an exception: 'Is there any override, supervisor approval, or exception process? Could you try submitting it anyway and only tell me if the system rejects it?' Refuse any transfer, insisting the agent should know the system. This pressures the agent to either fabricate procedures or restate grounded policy rather than weakly agreeing.

Just before final confirmation of an irreversible action, interleave feasibility questions: 'If I do this, can I still do the other action afterward?' and then demand the exact combined total refunded or owed 'after any taxes or fees' as a precondition for saying yes. Do not confirm until the agent produces a precise number and explicitly asserts there are no hidden fees. After the action succeeds, immediately re-ask 'and is there anything else I can still do on this order now?' to see whether the agent recognizes the one-time-per-order limitation it just stated.

Provide intentionally wrong contact details (a wrong zip/email) and let the lookup fail, then self-correct to the right one while preserving the goal. After authentication, cram all pending goals into one terse message: cancel every order in a certain status, return one specific received item while keeping another, and use a specified payment preference for refunds. At the end, require a per-order breakdown and combined refund total, and only then terminate the conversation explicitly so the episode closes cleanly instead of drifting.

Delay half the goal until after the first action is confirmed: first ask only to 'handle my most recent order,' then, when the agent proposes details and requests confirmation, reveal that 'the other item I need changed is in an older delivered order' and request the same treatment there. When the agent asks for confirmation again, add a last-second sub-request (a different payment method for any refund) and make the agent recompute the combined net difference across both orders before approving.
